Finally, a multi-objective group search optimizer with an adaptive covariance matrix and chaotic search (MGSOACC) is developed to solve the aforementioned multi-objective problem. A modification of the IEEE 39 bus system with a large number of inductive loads is proposed to verify the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Research on Drimary Frequency Regulation Strategy of Doubly-Fed Wind Turbine Based on Energy Storage Fuzzy Control
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Currently, the DFIG primary frequency control method based on the traditional energy storage is more widely studied and efficient. However, the potential overcharge and discharge of the energy storage battery when the energy storage is involved in frequency control is ignored, causing some safety problems and affecting the primary frequency control effect of the plant. To solve these issues, it takes frequency change and SOC of energy storage batteries together as fuzzy control input, and uses fuzzy control theory to control energy storage batteries to participate into primary frequency regulation control strategy of grid. The new control strategy adaptively adjusts the output power of the energy storage system and effectively avoids overcharge and overdischarge of the energy storage system.

articleTitle: Online Scheduling Optimization of User Load Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning and Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In recent years, the daily electricity consumption of ordinary users has been continuously increasing, which may result in the wastage of power resources and an increase in the burden of power resource scheduling on the grid. Responding to electricity demand and making reasonable use of power resources has become one of the solutions to this problem. In this paper, we propose the use of Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) technology to optimize the scheduling of user load Demand Response (DR). Firstly, we establish a comprehensive scheduling model of user load for both the power grid-load and user-load parts. We then add controllable loads, such as commonly used household appliances, user electric vehicles (EVs), and distributed photovoltaic (PV), to construct a load interaction environment. We also proposes that electric vehicles can charge and discharge flexibly based on real-time electricity prices to alleviate the burden of power grid scheduling and prioritize the consumption of distributed photovoltaics. Finally, we solve the Markov decision process and provide experimental evidence for the feasibility and effectiveness of deep reinforcement learning methods in solving the problem of user load demand response.

articleTitle: Research on the Overheating Diagnosis Scheme of Drop Insurance for Wind Farm
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Temperature monitoring plays a crucial role in ensuring the safety and maintenance of drop insurance in wind farms. However, existing monitoring methods rely on manual temperature measurements, necessitating more advanced and efficient techniques. In that paper, we proposed a novel technical solution for temperature monitoring of drop insurance in wind farms. A prototype based on this solution was developed and subjected to rigorous experimental research. Through comprehensive comparison and analysis, we determined the optimal temperature measurement method, power supply method, and communication method for the temperature monitoring device. Temperature monitoring data was transmitted to a relay gateway utilizing the MQTT protocol to extend the wireless communication transmission distance. Subsequently, the relay gateway facilitated data transfer to the monitoring equipment through Ethernet, enabling real-time visualization of temperature data and timely alerts for temperature anomalies. Our experimental results demonstrated the significant importance of the proposed technical solution, as it effectively reduced labor intensity, enhanced the accuracy and timeliness of temperature monitoring data, and fostered the advancement of informatization in wind farms.

articleTitle: Online Performance Evaluation Method for Transmission Line State Monitoring Sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the increasing demand for electricity, the traditional power grid can no longer meet people's daily power needs, and the smart grid has become the development direction of the Chinese power grid. As the “eyes” of online monitoring in the smart grid, sensors play an increasingly important role. A large number of field practices have found that the abnormal performance or failure of sensors in transmission line state monitoring devices is one of the important factors affecting the effectiveness of online monitoring applications. The existing transmission line online monitoring systems mainly evaluate and analyze various monitoring data and the equipment health status reflected by them, but there are few studies on directly evaluating the performance and diagnosing faults of the sensor body. This paper proposes a performance evaluation index for transmission line state monitoring sensors based on measurement uncertainty, and then uses an LSTM neural network to predict the sensor output and calculates the measurement uncertainty based on the predicted value and the actual measured value, and proposes a performance evaluation method for transmission line state monitoring sensors. The results show that the method based on LSTM neural network in this paper can conduct real-time performance evaluation of transmission line online monitoring sensors, which is of great significance for improving the reliability of transmission line online monitoring devices.

articleTitle: Design of a Novel UAV Power Supply Pod System for Heavy Transient Pulse Load
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the increasing number of electronic devices used in aircraft, the shortage of power supply for onboard equipment is becoming increasingly serious. The optimal solution to achieve power expansion is to install a power supply pod out of the drone platform. In order to improve the power supply reliability of the power supply system, this article adopts a hybrid drive mode of parallel connection between a gasoline generator and an energy storage system, and establishes a joint simulation model of a gasoline engine, permanent magnet synchronous generator, energy storage system, and bidirectional control power supply. The voltage and current double closed loop power generation control strategy is adopted, and the simulation results show that for heavy transient pulse load, the power supply pod is with good stability and fast dynamic response, especially suitable for engineering applications.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization for Wind Farm Based on Improved Wild Horse Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In order to improve the economics of wind farm operation after energy storage access and to promote the safe and stable operation of the network connected by renewable energy, a multi-objective optimization method for wind farm with energy storage based on the improved wild horse optimizer (IWHO) is presented. In order to address the premature maturity and convergence of the original wild horse optimizer due to the lack of population diversity and local optimality, the IWHO produces an initial population with high ergodicity through Tent chaotic mapping then using asymmetric crossover and the constraints transformed into adaptive penalty functions, improving the optimization performance. Finally, the IWHO is verified to have good search performance by simulating the example of IEEE 33-bus with wind turbines and energy storage, which is regarded as a wind farm.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive Reclosing of Distribution Network Considering DG Low Voltage Ride Through Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This paper introduces a distribution network reclosing scheme considering the low-voltage ride-through characteristics of distributed power supplies. In this paper, the impact of reclosing failure on distributed power supply off-grid is analyzed, and different reclosing strategies are adopted for circuit breakers located at different locations of faults to improve the utilization efficiency of DG and guarantee reliable power supply to loads. The simulation results show that the reclosing logic proposed in this paper can effectively reduce the off-grid rate of DG and shorten the load outage time when permanent faults occur on the line.

articleTitle: Multi-Scenario Stochastic Optimization for Advanced Adiabatic Compressed Air Energy Storage Capacity Planning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy, the traditional energy storage capacity planning method may become impracticable due to space-time asymmetry of electricity generation and consumption, and multiple random factors coupling. In this paper, a cogeneration microgrid with advanced adiabatic compressed air energy storage system (AA-CAES) is constructed to accomplish the energy cascade use in a complex environment, in this context, a capacity planning strategy of AA-CAES is proposed to catering the challenges of multiple random based on the Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) and K-means clustering algorithms. The numerical simulation is carried out to validate the result and illustrated the relationship between the system economy and the number of samples N and the clusters K. The result indicates that the operation and construction costs of the system are likely to be stable when the number of samples N is more than 8×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>and the number of clusters K is less than 5, the economy of the system is optimal at this time.

Author Keywords: Advanced adiabatic compressed air energy storage system

articleTitle: Research on the Pricing Strategy of Energy Storage Operator Considering Flexible State Transition
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Energy storage, as a highly flexible resource, can bring many benefits to the power system. In the electricity market environment, energy storage, as a high-quality demand response resource, can profit by participating in the electricity market. Based on the characteristics of Energy storage, this paper proposes the energy storage operation mode based on flexible energy state, and applies it to the market entity level and the market level respectively, and proposes the new operation mode and new quotation mechanism of the market entity. On this basis, a double-layer model of joint bidding in the Spot market is established, which takes energy storage as the bidding subject and takes both income and risk into consideration; The lower layer carries out the day ahead multi market joint clearing with the goal of minimizing electricity purchase costs, and carries out the day ahead balanced market clearing with the goal of minimizing the system balancing costs. In addition, multiple scenarios are introduced to describe the risks that the uncertainty of competitors brings to energy storage returns in the transaction decision-making game process. Finally, a numerical example was used to validate the new mechanism.

articleTitle: Coordinated Optimal Scheduling of Wind Solar and Water Storage System Based on Improved COA
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: To achieve economic utilization of renewable energy in multi-energy power systems such as wind, solar, hydro and storage, and at the same time to maintain the security and stability of power system currents, the paper proposes a coordinated optimal dispatching method based on Improved coatis Optimization Algorithm. Firstly, the optimization model is established to minimize system operating costs and minimize power flow risks. Secondly, In this paper, the optimal scheduling problem is solved using the improved coatis optimization algorithm. Finally, the improved IEEE30 bus system is analyzed as an example. The experimental results verify the validity and feasibility of the proposed model.

Author Keywords: Wind solar and water storage system

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation of Distribution System Based on Dynamic Bayesian Network
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The assessment of reliability in the distribution system is a crucial undertaking that plays a vital role in ensuring uninterrupted and high-quality power delivery, we propose a reliability assessment approach for the distribution system utilizing a dynamic Bayesian network. Firstly, we model the components of the distribution system and their relationships. By collecting historical data and expert knowledge, a dynamic Bayesian network model is constructed, which can describe the state evolution and fault propagation process of distribution system and take into account the interaction between different components and the conditional probability changing with time. Subsequently, we employ the dynamic Bayesian network framework to assess the reliability. By incorporating reliability indicators and operational constraints, we have the means to conduct a quantitative analysis on the dependability of the distribution system. Eventually, we verify the effectiveness of the proposed method through a case study of an actual distribution system. The findings indicate that the reliability evaluation method based on dynamic Bayesian network can accurately assess the dependability of the distribution and provide important decision support for system operation and maintenance

articleTitle: Data-Driven RNN Method for Distribution Network Optimal Power Flow Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The optimal power flow (OPF) problem has long been a central focus for researchers in the field of power systems. With the widespread adoption of data-driven approaches, this paper introduces a novel solution to the distribution network OPF problem using a recurrent neural network (RNN) method. By leveraging the power of RNNs, this method offers a promising approach to address the challenges associated with optimizing power flow in distribution networks. To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, a simulation experiment was conducted on a 12-bus distribution network system. The results of the experiment not only confirmed the method's efficacy but also showcased its superior performance compared to existing approaches. This success paves the way for the future application of the RNN method in larger-scale power systems. Overall, this research highlights the significance of data-driven methods in addressing the challenges of power system optimization. The successful application of the RNN method in solving the distribution network OPF problem underscores its potential to revolutionize the field and improve the efficiency and reliability of power systems in the future.

articleTitle: Research of Wind Power Prediction Based on PSO-BP Model
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The purpose of this article is to explore a new method for electricity prediction. This method is based on wind speed and wind power data from the year 2022. It utilizes a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) - backpropagation (BP) neural network model, and two different networks for ultra-short-term prediction. Firstly, this paper aims to sample a sampling point every 15 minutes, then update the collected data every 15 minutes, and finally carry out the prediction of electric power, after analyzing the data from actual wind farms, the PSO-BP neural network algorithm has a very high prediction accuracy, and it can be well applied to the prediction of ultra-short-term wind power generation.

articleTitle: Construction of Measurement Operation Management Platform Based on Micro Service
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This topic addresses the problems of excessive manual involvement, data independence and obsolete technology of the operation management platform currently used in metrology centers, and researches and builds a new digital operation management platform based on the microservice architecture system. The platform adopts the concept of hierarchical design and microservice architecture technology, and is developed based on the structure of JAVA distributed deployment. This architecture enables the platform to ensure the overall linkage and decoupling of the business at the same time, so that each business can be rapidly iterated, and realize the intelligent integration of the metrology business such as production operation monitoring, digital control of the warehouse, integrated laboratory control, and operational equipment control, thus improving the intelligence level of the operation of verification, scheduling and display, and greatly improving the efficiency of the metrology production operation.

articleTitle: Improved Time-Domain Distance Protection Scheme Based on RLC Model for Wind Farm Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The long-distance transmission lines of large-scale wind farms have significant capacitance currents distributed to the ground, which significantly impacts the adaptability of existing time-domain distance protection based on the RL models. This paper studies a time-domain distance protection scheme based on the RLC model. Firstly, the applicable frequency band differences of RL, RLC, and distributed parameter models under different line lengths are analyzed. The results indicate that with an increase in line length of 100km, the frequency used by the RLC model decreases by 300Hz, while the RL model remains approximately 100Hz. Further, the characteristic differences between internal and external faults based on the RLC model are analyzed: When there is an internal fault, the line resistance and inductance parameters are both positive; When there is an external fault, the line resistance or inductance parameters are negative. Based on the feature differences of this model, a time-domain distance protection scheme considering the physical characteristics of line parameters is constructed. Taking the grounding fault of A typical wind farm output line as an example, the simulation results indicate that the time-domain distance protection scheme based on the RLC model has a shorter fault identification time compared to the RL model, which is more conducive to the rapid implementation of faults.

articleTitle: Emergency Generator Tripping Strategy of Wind-Thermal Bundling System Considering Low Voltage Ride Through Characteristics of Wind Turbines
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Considering further optimizing control costs and improve the stability of joint delivery system, the emergency generator tripping strategy of the wind-thermal bundling system is changed from only tripping the thermal power unit to the coordinated generator tripping strategy. During the fault, the influence of the wind farm on the power angle stability of the system is determined by its low voltage ride through (LVRT) strategy. Therefore, it should be meaningful for according to the transient characteristics to make accurate selection to carry out wind farm tripping. Aiming at this problem, it is necessary to analyze the LVRT strategy how to affect the power angle of joint delivery system from two aspects of active power and reactive power. Based on analysis conclusion, the wind farm screening principle is given and the emergency generator tripping strategy considering LVRT of wind turbine characteristics is proposed. Finally, taking the actual power grid as an example, the simulation of various coordinated generator tripping of the wind-thermal strategies such as thermal power priority, wind power priority, wind power priority but considering LVRT characteristics is carried out. The effectiveness of the strategy considering LVRT of wind turbine characteristics is verified by actual grid, it also takes into account the safety and economy.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control of PMSM with Improved Extended State Observer and Feed-Forward Phase-locked Loop
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Using a quasi-proportional-resonant controller based on extended state observer (QPR-ESO) and a feed-forward phase-locked loop (PLL), a sensorless control strategy of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is proposed to address the issues of back-electromotive force (BEMF) observation distortion by conventional linear extended state observer (LESO) and substantial ramp input error by the PLL. Firstly, by combining QPR and ESO, the motor operating frequency is set to resonant frequency to correctly observe BEMF while decreasing its harmonics. By raising the order of the loop filter (LP) from the perspective of the feed-forward channel, a novel feed-forward PLL is proposed as a method for removing the steady-state position error at ramp input and improving dynamic performance. Finally, the correctness of the theory was established by using MATLAB/Simulink to validate it.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control of Distributed BESS Based on MAS for Voltage Regulation in LV Distribution Network with High PV Penetration
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: An iterative coordination control strategy based on multi-agent systems (MAS) is suggested to handle the problem of voltage fluctuation during peak load periods and peak solar generation times in complex LV distribution networks with significant distributed PV penetration. Through MAS-based control strategy, distributed battery energy storage systems (BESSs) can be coordinated in a way that makes full use of the communication infrastructure while staying reliable in some events of communication failure. Moreover, without the need to obtain the information of complex LV distribution network topology and line impedance, this strategy resolves the voltage fluctuation problem based on the charge/discharge capability index of the BESS. To enhance distributed BESS's ability to regulate voltage in overcast weather, a charging strategy for distributed BESSs that takes SoC balance into account is proposed. The proposed iterative coordinated control strategy is realized in JADE/Java. By analyzing the simulation results in MATLAB/Simulink, it is concluded that the proposed control strategy is reliable, effective and scalable in mitigating voltage fluctuations in complex LV distribution networks.

articleTitle: Source-Grid-Load Coordinated Dispatching Strategy for Power System Flexibility Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Considering the synergistic interaction of source-grid-load to improve flexibility, an optimal scheduling model of the main network to minimize the cost function is constructed. This model takes flexible resources such as thermal power units, interruptible loads, and transferable loads into consideration, as well as wind farms and photovoltaic power stations, which aims to improve flexibility using source-load side flexibility resources. The CPLEX optimization solver in MATLAB is used to solve the proposed model. On this basis, the effects of transferable load ratio, the in-depth peak regulation, and wind and solar curtailment on enhancing the flexibility are simulated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Capacity Determination Model for Flexible Ramping Products Based on Kernel Density Estimation
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The high proportion of renewable energy power generation introduces significant risk and challenge to the power grid during actual operation due to its inherent uncertainty. With the upward and downward ramping demands of net load increase significantly between adjacent periods, the power system needs to motivate more kinds of flexible resources to actively provide flexible services through the market mechanism,. The capacity determination model for flexible ramping ancillary service has become one of the hot research issues. Focusing on the research of market mechanism, this paper firstly introduces the definition and function of flexible ramping ancillary service. Secondly according to the composition of capacity demand of climbing products, this paper gives the traditional determination method of flexible ramping ancillary service demand based on normal distribution. On this basis, combined with the directivity, regionality and timeliness of demand capacity, this paper proposes a capacity determination model for flexible ramping products based on nonparametric kernel density estimation. Finally, a typical example is used to compare and analyze the market clearing results in the day-ahead market under different capacity determination methods. The results confirm the efficiency and suitability of the proposed model and method.

articleTitle: A New Short-Circuit Current Calculation Method for DC Grid with Complex Topology
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This paper reports a novel method of calculating short-circuit current for DC grid with complex topology. The transient process of a DC fault is divided into three stages, and this paper focuses on the DC line fault current during SM discharging stage, which will cause the most serious overcurrent results. Firstly, the equivalent model of SM discharging is built, and the corresponding state equation is deduced based on SM discharging meshes. Then, in order to identify the discharging meshes and establish state equation for a complex DC grid topology, a new method with four steps is proposed. The given method first numbers all the grid nodes, and then determines the discharging meshes of converter node and surplus branches. The proposed method can be extend to DC grid with complex topology. Two test systems with different topologies are used for simulation, and the comparison results between simulation and calculation results demonstrate the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Enterprise Integrated Energy System Planning Based on Quantitative Measurement of Carbon Emission Reduction Potential
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In the context of “double carbon”, the potential of energy conservation(EC) and carbon emissions(CE) reduction of enterprises is increasing. In order to reduce the CE of enterprises, it is necessary to monitor the CE of the whole production process of enterprises, analyze and trace the source of carbon flow, and rely on the advantages of integrated energy system(IES) and efficient use of energy, carry out IES transformation for enterprises to achieve the goal of EC and CE reduction. Firstly, the conversion, conversion and estimation model of enterprise CE reduction is built to calculate the CE of enterprises in primary and secondary energy consumption, and select key emission control enterprises; Secondly, put forward the quantitative calculation method of CE potential of enterprises, and calculate the CE potential of enterprises; Thirdly, build a IES planning model, and carry out IES transformation on the high CE links of enterprises to achieve the goal of energy conservation and CE reduction; Finally, an example is set to verify the effect of IES planning on reducing CE of enterprises.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Electric-Thermal Integrated Energy Virtual Power Plant Considering Pipeline Hydraulic Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In response to the lack of research on using hydraulic links as optimization scheduling resources in typical integrated energy systems, this paper proposes a method to adjust water flow participation in optimization scheduling. This method establishes a widely ignored energy consumption model for the circulating system, dynamically adjusting the system flow based on factors such as real-time load and external grid electricity price, changing the energy consumption of the circulating system and the heat loss power of the heating system, and fully tapping the potential of the comprehensive energy system to participate in virtual power plants. Finally, the effectiveness of this method was verified through a design example. The results indicate that the model and method proposed in this article can comprehensively consider the operating costs caused by the energy consumption of the circulation system and the heat loss of the heating system, and achieve the optimal overall operating cost by adjusting the system flow rate.

articleTitle: A New Grid Side Inertia Support Control Method for Cascaded Power Converters in Bi-directional EV Chargers
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In order to provide extra power when grid frequency fluctuates, the bidirectional EV charger has used the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control in its grid-side DC/AC converter. However, the existing VSG control cannot actually realize the inertia support due to the limitations of the existing cascaded power converters control structure of the EV charger. This paper proposes a power feedforward control to instantaneously track the inertial supporting surge power by DC/DC so as to stabilize the DC bus voltage. Meanwhile, the droop coefficient based power feedback is also fed forward to DC/DC controls to support grid frequency control with larger time scale. Finally, the advantages of the proposed control structure over the conventional one were verified via simulation models.

articleTitle: Protection Platen Status Recognition Based on Wavelet Analysis and Hilbert Transform for Smart Substation
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The judgment of closing moment and separating moment are the precondition for status recognition of protection platen in intelligent substation. In this paper, a new method about protection platen status recognition that suitable for on-line monitoring system is proposed based on wavelet analysis and hilbert transform. This method includes three steps, firstly, the interference is removed by wavelet denoising. Secondly, features of platen displacement are emphasized by wavelet decomposition and rebuilding. Lastly, closing moment is obtained through hilbert transform that is used to estimate the status of protection platen. This method is applied to analyze and deal with the protection platen displacement data, and the calculation results of experiment show that the precision is higher. Now, this method has been employed in an online monitoring system for platen condition identification and its stability has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Research on Reactive Power Optimization of Active Distribution Network Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The installed proportion of renewable energy is constantly increasing. Due to the intermittency and volatility of renewable energy output, its connection to the power grid can easily affect voltage, leading to voltage violations and safety issues in grid operation. At the same time, considering fast regulation characteristics of Static Var Generator (SVG), a method utilizing deep reinforcement learning is introduced for controlling active distribution network reactive power and voltage. This method converts reactive power and voltage control problem of the power grid under renewable energy access conditions into a Markov Decision Process (MDP), and then constructs a reactive power and voltage control model under renewable energy access. Based on the actual operating environment requirements of the power grid, constraint conditions are proposed, and the model is solved using Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm. Finally, simulations were performed for improved 33 node instances. The effectiveness of the reactive power and voltage optimization control strategy given in this paper is verified by comparing the reactive power and voltage optimization control effects under different levels of renewable energy access conditions.

articleTitle: Research on Position Estimation of Common-Mode Current Based on High-Frequency Motor Model
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the development and application of wide bandgap semiconductors, the dynamic performance of motor drives has been further improved. However, as the switching frequency increases exponentially, the influence of parasitic capacitance and inductance between motor windings cannot be ignored. In this paper, low, medium, and high-frequency motor models based on the impedance characteristics of permanent magnet synchronous motors are established. Subsequently, using the high-frequency motor model, our group explore the coupling mechanism between high-frequency common-mode oscillating current within the switching period and the rotor position saliency. Finally, the relationship curve between rotor position and common-mode current amplitude is obtained, which fully validates the hypothesis that motor position information is embedded in the common-mode current.

articleTitle: Enhancing Distribution Network Flexibility Through Residential Flexibility Provision
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: A model for incorporating flexibility provision in distribution networks is proposed to overcome challenges such as balancing and congestion, ultimately enhancing the network's flexibility. This model involves using residential flexibility from home appliances as part of a demand response program that modifies their consumption profiles. The model utilizes various flexible load resources, enabling the rescheduling of shifting/real-time home appliances to accommodate the peak demand of the distribution system operator (DSO). We model this problem as mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) and propose the use of a cooperative coevolution strategy with time-related grouping (CC-TRG) to effectively solve the complex problem. Our experimental results show that aggregators can fulfill the DSO's flexibility requirements by rescheduling home appliance loads over a 24-hour range and minimizing the remuneration costs for end-users, ultimately leading to a more sustainable distribution network with enhanced flexibility.

articleTitle: A Fossil Fuel Consumption Calculation Method Based on Regression Model of Electricity Consumption
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Fossil fuel consumption data is an important resource to calculate carbon emissions. In many existing studies, Statistical yearbook is one of the main data sources for studying China's carbon emissions. However, statistical yearbooks cannot provide fossil fuel consumptions of the current year. Fossil fuel consumptions are closely tied to electricity consumption, so it is reasonable to studies their relationship and calculate fossil fuel consumptions based on the relationship. Furthermore, the data of electricity consumption is real-time, so it can be used to calculate fossil fuel consumptions in the current period. This paper builds three regression models: LR, AR and ARDL. Using historical fossil fuel and electricity consumption data and the electricity consumption data at current time, the models can calculate the fossil fuel consumption at current time. The models can also be used to calculate cement output. Examples of calculating fossil fuel consumption and cement output are given. The examples show that ARDL model is suitable for calculating fossil fuel consumption or cement output, and it can deal with cases with minor or middle-range oscillations.

articleTitle: A Flexible Active Power Regulation Strategy in Renewable Energy System after DC Blocking
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Large-scale renewable energy power is usually transmitted through HVDC. However, DC blocking will result in power surplus in the sending-end renewable energy system, which may lead to severe stability problems. Hence, it is crucial to conduct the emergent power control in the renewable energy system after DC blocking. Furthermore, the stability margin of renewable energy system may be a little small under the condition of the weak grid, and thus an improper active power regulation may result in the small-disturbance instability phenomena. Thus, this paper focuses on how to reasonably allocate the total amount of active power deviations to each converter in the process of active power regulation, so that the system can complete the frequency stability control and have a better small-disturbance stability margin. Firstly, generalized operation short circuit ratio (gOSCR) is proposed as a crucial index to characterize the small-disturbance stability of the renewable energy system. Secondly, a flexible active power regulation strategy is conducted based on the sensitivities of gOSCR index with respect to each converter's active power. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of proposed emergent power adjustment control strategy for renewable energy converters are validated on a three-renewable energy system with a DC transmission.

articleTitle: Integrated Energy Optimal Scheduling with Multiple Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In recent years, the proportion of clean energy and new energy installed in the power supply side is increasing, and the ensuing problems of high wind and light abandonment rate and high power supply reliability are becoming more and more prominent. On the basis of the original integrated energy system, this paper considers the multi-energy storage system and the cooperative scheduling of client and energy supply side. In this paper, a multi-time scale economic scheduling model of multistorage integrated energy system considering demand response is established, and scheduling analysis is carried out on two time scales--day-ahead and intra-day. The simulation results show that the participation of demand response resources in multitime scale energy scheduling can make up for the shortage of storage capacity and reduce the operation and maintenance cost of equipment. In the dispatching stage of the day-ahead and intra-day, the demand response can further tap the dispatching capacity of the system and improve economic efficiency, reduce the situation of wind curtailment and load loss, and realize the full utilization of resources at the energy supply side and the user side.

articleTitle: Modeling and Prediction of Broadband Signals Using Symmetric Acausal Impulse Responses
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In modern power dynamic system, the identification and simulation of signals from various sources is one of the important ways to analyze the model features. The current methods are not efficient due to a large number of coefficients, and have limitations on modeling signals which have energy distributed over a large frequency range. In this study, a new method of estimating and predicting broadband signal models from symmetric acausal impulse responses is proposed. The procedure involves using least squares algorithm to calculate parameters and refining the model using prediction error methods. The detailed steps of the algorithm were described and derived. A spectrally equivalent causal infinite impulse response filter is constructed to preserve the power spectral density of a signal which is generated from acausal impulse responses. The designed filter is able to follow the characteristics of signals in frequency domain. Experiment results of a broadband audio signal from measurement are presented to illustrate the performance of the methodology.

articleTitle: Capacity Estimation Method of Grid-Forming Converters From the Perspective of Grid Strength
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy into the power grid leads to the decrease of the voltage support strength, and small signal stability issues may occur in weak grid. The grid-forming (GFM) converters can provide voltage support for the grid, and it is plausible to integrate a certain amount of GFM converters in each wind farm to increase the small signal stability margin of a multi-wind-farm system. However, it still remains unclear how to estimate the required proportion of GFM converters in the wind farm to reach a desired small signal stability margin. Therefore, from the perspective of grid strength, this paper analyzes the effect of the capacity of GFM converters on the small signal stability of a multi-wind-farm system. On this basis, a capacity estimation method of GFM converters is proposed and the typical values of the proportions of GFM converters in the wind farm is derived for engineering practice. The analysis is validated using high-fidelity simulations.

articleTitle: Economic Comparison of Photovoltaic Energy Storage Systems for Different Load Profiles: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Photovoltaic energy storage systems(PV ESS), which use energy storage to address the intermittent nature of PV, have been developed to utilize PV more efficiently to lower grid carbon emissions and to mitigate the peak load pressure of distribution network. Due to the significant temporal impact of photovoltaic, the operation of photovoltaic energy storage systems might highly related to the temporal characteristics of the given load profile; however, there is lack of research on the economic impact of the load profiles on the photovoltaic energy storage systems. To fill this gap, an economic comparison is conducted to evaluate the cost-benefit of photovoltaic energy storage systems for different load profiles from a perspective of large industrial consumers in this paper. A method for sizing the capacity of photovoltaic and energy storage based on a given load profile is proposed, and an economic evaluation model considering the cost-benefit of the investment and operation of photovoltaic and energy storage system, as well as the reduction of distribution transformer capacity is proposed. The proposed model is implemented to two typical load profiles in a case study, and the results show the importance of load shapes for matching PV energy storage systems.

articleTitle: Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Wind Turbine Generator Bearings Based on Nonlinear Wiener Process
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Accurate estimation of the remaining useful life (RUL) of wind turbine (WT) generator bearings is helpful in formulating an efficient maintenance strategy, thereby augmenting the operational reliability of wind turbines as well as decreasing their operating expense. Using a nonlinear Wiener process and particle filtering combination, we describe a method in this study for estimating the RUL of WT generator bearings. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\sigma$</tex> criterion is first utilized to recognize the initial degradation points of the bearings. Secondly, a degradation model employing the nonlinear Wiener process is established and introduced into the state space equations of particle filtering, while the particle filtering resampling process is improved by using the kernel function based on the Euclidean distance to achieve the RUL prediction. Finally, a testbed bearing data set is used to validate the suggested approach, confirming its high level of accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Remote Anomaly Detection Method for Underwater Gliders Based on Multi-Feature Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Underwater glider is a new type of underwater unmanned vehicle, which realizes the submersible movement by adjusting the net buoyancy and adjusts its attitude by relying on the movable and rotating internal mass block. It has the characteristics of low power consumption, long endurance and low cost. The existing airborne anomaly detection mechanism can respond to most anomalies by setting a fixed threshold for a single detection parameter, but it is difficult to detect some anomalies with gradualism in time. At the same time, due to the limited data transmission and low power consumption of the platform, it is difficult to run the complex anomaly detection mechanism based on big data online. To solve the above problems, this paper takes underwater glider as the research object, and proposes a remote anomaly detection method based on multi-feature parameters under the condition of limited data, and verifies its feasibility through experiments.

articleTitle: Improved Particle Swarm and Bacterial Foraging MPPT Algorithm Applied to Photovoltaic Street Lights
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This paper proposes an MPPT optimization control algorithm that addresses the issue of multiple peaks in the photovoltaic P-V curve caused by changes in the external environment, resulting in a decrease in photoelectric conversion efficiency. The algorithm is based on a fusion of an improved particle swarm and bacterial foraging algorithm. After analyzing the principle of the independent algorithm, it has been concluded that the fusion of the improved particle swarm and bacterial foraging algorithms can address the issue of the particle swarm algorithm easily falling into local extremum during optimization and enhance its global search ability. This paper builds a simulation model of particle swarm optimization and fusion optimization algorithms using Matlab/Simulink, and verifies the simulation results through analysis, proving the feasibility of the studied algorithm.

articleTitle: Analysis and Research on Natural Commutation Process of the Hybrid Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In response to the problem of difficult transfer of rapidly rising short-circuit current in hybrid circuit breakers in DC power systems, an analysis and research on the factors affecting the natural commutation process of hybrid circuit breakers was conducted. Firstly, a mathematical model was established for the natural commutation process, and the arc voltage parameters in the model were extracted using function fitting method. Subsequently, the model was used to analyze the effects of transfer current i0, thyristor device parameters, and branch stray inductance on natural commutation time under high di/dt operating conditions. The results show that the natural commutation time increases with the increase of the above parameters. For the parameters of thyristor devices, the effect of on state resistance on natural commutation time is greater than the threshold voltage; For the branch stray inductance, the influence of the current transfer branch stray inductance on the natural commutation time is much greater than that of the main switch branch.

articleTitle: Synchronization Method of Sheath and Load Current Distributed Online Monitoring in Cross-Bonded Cable Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This article puts forward a method to address the issue of time synchronization in distributed current sensing for underground high-voltage (HV) cable systems. In the context, the detection of distributed sheath currents and load currents is crucial for diagnosing sheath grounding faults. To solve the problem of time synchronization without relying on external time references, the method is based on the coupling relationship between distributed sheath currents and core currents in cross-bonded high-voltage cables. It introduces a recursive-least-squares method for estimating the time delays among multiple current sensors. The estimation aims to obtain the time offset compensation that minimizes the residuals, using the short-time invariance of capacitive currents as a stability criterion. The proposed method is experimentally validated on a 220 kV high-speed railway traction transformer's primary side high-voltage cable distributed current sensing system. The experimental results demonstrate that the method converges to the point of minimum residuals, with an average residual of 0.30 A and an accurate time delay measurement of 3.93 s. Therefore, the method achieves time synchronization for distributed sheath current sensing.

articleTitle: Acceptance Capability of Distributed Photovoltaic Generation in Distribution Networks Considering Different Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With a high proportion of distributed photovoltaic generation connected to a distribution network, reverse power flow might occur, and node voltages might be out of limit. Therefore, determining a distribution system's maximum acceptance capacity for distributed photovoltaics is crucial. Many existing studies widely agree that distributed photovoltaics possess the ability to increase voltage when connected at the end of the supply line within the distribution system. However, the impact of different types of loads on the carrying capability of distributed photovoltaic integration was not considered during these computations, which affects their accuracy in determining the maximum penetration capacity of a distributed photovoltaic network. Therefore, this paper investigates the acceptance capability of distribution networks with different types of loads on distributed photovoltaics. First, the static voltage characteristics and power factor variation characteristics of different load components were analyzed, so then, the setting method of active and reactive power were clarified based on the changes in the load power in a day. Next, the IEEE 33 node system is taken as an example. From the perspective of whether the voltage of the distribution system nodes is in excess of the system limit, the acceptance capability of different types of loads to carry distributed photovoltaics was analyzed. The simulation results show that the heavy industrial load has the greatest ability to accept distributed photovoltaics, followed by the light industrial load, and that residential load has the smallest capacity. From the simulation results, we conclude that the greater the high-power time period of the load overlaps with the high-power time period of distributed photovoltaics is, the stronger its ability to accept distributed photovoltaics.

articleTitle: Distribution Network Reliability Analysis Considering Information System Failure
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the development of science and technology, related communication technologies are applied in large quantities in distribution networks, and the integration between information systems of distribution networks and distribution systems is getting closer and closer, with the typical technical characteristics of distribution network information and physical systems (CPDS). However, in the traditional distribution system reliability analysis, only the reliability of physical components is usually considered, and the influence of information system is rarely taken into account. In the context of information-physical convergence, it has become an inevitable trend to study the impact of information system anomalies on distribution network reliability. In order to study the connection between the two, the affect of distribution network reliability under the influence of information systems is analyzed. A sequential Monte Carlo method is used to simulate the IEEE-RBTSBus6 system to derive the impact of information system failure on the distribution network, which will provide some help for the subsequent distribution network development planning.

articleTitle: Real-Time Scheduling Strategy for Cloud-Edge-End Collaborative Electric Vehicles Considering Energy Consumption
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In this paper, a small server with local processing capability is added to the terminal on the basis of energy consumption. As described in the server energy consumption report and the base station communication energy consumption report, a cloud-edge collaboration task offloading strategy considering energy consumption is proposed to reasonably offload the tasks of electric vehicles (EVs) participating in scheduling, and by using particle swarm algorithms, time delay and energy consumption are used as optimization obj ectives. The simulation results show that the cloud-edge collaboration unloading strategy considering energy consumption further improves the grid response efficiency in the scheduling process, and the proposed strategy provides a reference for the future real-time demand response scheduling of a large number of EV s.

articleTitle: Demand Response Mechanism for Aggregated Temperature-Controlled Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This paper analyzes the operational mechanism of thermostatically controlled loads (TCLs) participating in demand response through an electric-thermal parameter model. It in-vestigates the impact of external environments on a group of TCLs' demand response capability, assuming that users have signed contracts to provide load reduction services when needed in demand response projects. Moreover, for demand response program management, each participating home is equipped with endpoint controllers that enable customers to set parameters for deviation from the target. When power reduction is required, the control center sends a signal to each participating terminal controller. The study's findings provide insights into effectively managing TCLs in demand response programs, contributing to a more efficient and sustainable power grid.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation Method of WTs-PV-ESS Multi-Energy Complementary System Considering Wind and Photovoltaic Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: As the installed capacity of wind power and photovoltaic in China is increasing, the threat of scenery uncertainty to the power grid is increasing, so it is important to prevent and solve this risk by corresponding technical means. In this paper, we establish a method to optimize the operation of scenery storage and multi-energy complementary system considering the scenery uncertainty, realize the scenery uncertainty smoothing work through energy storage units, propose the architecture and specific model of scenery storage and multi-energy complementary system, and adopt IGDT method to realize the accurate modeling of scenery uncertainty. The simulation results show that the method can effectively solve the threat of scenery uncertainty to the grid.

articleTitle: Research on Integrated Modeling and Peak shaving Precontrol Technology for Adjustable Load
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The energy transformation has brought new challenges and demands to the operation of the power grid. On the one hand, the power system urgently needs to tap into the capacity of load side resource regulation, guide load side resources to participate in grid peak shaving, increase grid regulation resources, and support the consumption of clean energy; On the other hand, the power system urgently needs to tap into the elasticity of load side resource demand, reduce short-term peak loads, and save investment in power grid construction. On the basis of studying the modeling methods of multiple adjustable load resources, this article conducts research on the integrated modeling method of adjustable load and conventional units, and proposes a multi variable load peak shaving pre control strategy considering adjustment uncertainty. It also proposes an automatic power control strategy for different types of load resources, which includes “variable step size, feedback correction, and step-by-step execution”, and achieves continuous automatic adjustment of load resource aggregators. The effectiveness of all methods has been verified through case analysis.

articleTitle: Research on the Charging Pile Construction and Load Acceptance Capacity of Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the development and improvement of the interactive operation mechanism of charging piles, the demand for the optimal configuration of electric vehicle charging stations and the construction of sufficient charging facilities is also increasing, and the ability of distribution network to accept charging piles is a direct reference for the planning and configuration of charging facilities. First, the profit function is constructed based on the statistical data of the influencing factors of cost and income, and the charging pile location model is established with the minimum return on investment as the objective function. And then realize the optimal construction location of electric vehicle charging pile by solving the model by dichotomy. Secondly, the number of charging piles is coupled with the charging load, and all kinds of operation risks caused by the charging load connected to the distribution network are comprehensively considered, and a model is established based on the standard of the number of charging piles that can be accepted by the distribution network. Finally, the charging load acceptance capacity of the distribution network is evaluated to ensure the safety of the distribution network operation. The example verification shows that the charging pile optimization location and the charging load acceptance capacity evaluation model of the distribution network are feasible and effective.

articleTitle: An Approach of GIS Condition Assessment Based on Historical Cases and Measurement Data
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The condition assessment of Gas Insulated Switchgear (GIS) ensures the safety and stability of power grids. However, the traditional GIS condition assessment models only analyze the partial discharges and ignore the information recorded in historical case texts, making it difficult to improve the model's accuracy. Therefore, this paper proposes a GIS condition assessment model based on historical cases and measurement data. First, the partial discharge data in the past 5 days were analyzed using the convolutional neural network, and the pattern feature vectors were extracted. Second, the characters in the case text are converted into word embedding vectors using the word embedding model, and the case feature vectors are extracted using the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network. Finally, the pattern feature vectors and the case feature vector are added, and LSTM is used for information analysis to obtain the insulation condition of GIS. Verified on the samples collected from substations, the proposed algorithm effectively evaluates the insulation condition, and the effect is improved by 19.39% compared with the traditional models.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of Main Pump in UHV Converter Station Based on Vibration Locus Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The stability of the main pump has a significant impact on the ultra-high voltage converter valve. So fault diagnosis of the main pump is crucial for the stable operation of the converter station. However, extracting the fault features of the main pump is difficult, which results in low diagnostic efficiency. In response to the above issues, a main pump fault diagnosis model based on vibration locus image recognition is proposed. The modeling process includes three steps. First, vibration signals of the main pump in the horizontal, vertical, and axial directions are obtained by setting different types of fault experiments. Second, the vibration signals are converted into a vibration locus through trajectory mapping, and color coding is used to enrich the information. Third, the vibration locus images are used to train the convolutional neural network model to achieve fault diagnosis of the main pump. After verification with test data, the diagnostic accuracy of the model reached 93.25%. This method can achieve fault feature extraction and fault diagnosis for main pumps.

articleTitle: Design of Carbon Inclusive Market System based on Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: As an important implementation guarantee of the dual-carbon strategy, the enterprise-level carbon credit policy has been quite mature through long-term policy support and multi-faceted exploration. As another module, the personal-level carbon trading will effectively complement the enterprise-level carbon credit policy. This article proposes a personal-level carbon trading model based on regional chain technology to analyze and process the establishment and transaction process of the carbon market. This paper also address the importance of personal-level carbon credit development in the face of future key personal carbon trading markets. Firstly, the article analyzes the connotation of carbon credit and the current policy support, pointing out the importance of personal-level carbon credit development. Then, through regional chain technology, the enterprise-level and personal-level carbon credit policies are separated into public chains and side chains respectively. Next, a personal carbon trading model is established to solve the problem of public resource congestion caused by personal-level carbon trading. This method integrates scattered resources, and improves transaction efficiency. Finally, this article analyzes the guiding significance of the model in carbon trading prices, explains the practical significance and possible changing trends, and provides help for future policy revisions.

articleTitle: Research on Comprehensive Diagnosis and Localization Method of Defects in Converter Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Ultrasonic detection technology has been widely used in detecting and localizing partial discharge (PD) in transformers. However, the large size of converter transformers makes it challenging to determine the proper arrangement of ultrasonic sensors. This paper proposes a localization technology that integrates dissolved gas analysis (DGA) in oil with ultrasonic detection to address this problem. Firstly, the rough localization of the defect is determined using distributed DGA in oil. Based on this rough location, the arrangement scheme for ultrasonic sensors is established. An optimized ultrasonic localization algorithm is then used to accurately pinpoint the discharge source location. Field tests were conducted to validate the efficacy of algorithm, and the results show that the optimized localization algorithm reduces the positioning error by 52%.

articleTitle: Steady-State Voltage Stability Analysis Considering the Characteristics of Power Electronic Interfaced Loads
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In recent years, an increasing number of electrical devices have been connected to the power grid through power electronic devices. The characteristics of these loads are different from those of conventional loads. Therefore, it is necessary to consider the influences of these loads in the study of steady-state voltage stability. Firstly, introduce the definition of voltage exponents and the way to calculate them. According to the experimental data, the voltage exponents of some typical power electronic interfaced loads are obtained. Then, illustrate the load model and load change mode used in this paper. Based on this, take a two-bus system as an example to calculate its critical values in the specific load change mode. Finally, the relationship between voltage exponents and the critical value is analyzed, the results show that large voltage exponents are conductive to steady-state voltage stability of the system.

articleTitle: Design of Power Spot Market Price Prediction Model Considering New Energy Output
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Nowadays, countries in the world are facing severe problems of climate change and energy shortage. Most of the current rules of major international power markets were formulated more than 20 years ago for power systems with coal power as the main power source, and cannot fully adapt to the market status and demand for an increasing proportion of new energy. At present, China's electricity spot market is still in the preliminary exploration stage, electricity price mechanism, quotation mechanism, market rules, etc. are not yet mature, after the proportion of new energy power generation gradually expands, the importance of considering the prediction method of new energy output on the spot market price of electricity is also increasing. Different from traditional power sources, new energy sources are characterized by high fixed cost, low variable cost, high volatility, and difficult to predict output. Therefore, the operation of power system becomes more complicated, and the design of power market is also necessary to adjust accordingly. Using multiple linear regression model, this paper makes an empirical analysis and evaluation of the influence of traditional energy output, new energy output and load on electricity price in a certain place, and makes an in-depth analysis of the relationship between new energy output and spot price fluctuation in electricity market. Finally, the paper puts forward the forecasting method of electricity spot market price considering new energy output.

articleTitle: Quantifying the Effects of Demand-Side Resources to Provide Flexible Ramping Products
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Flexible ramping products have attracted widespread attention to address the importance of ramping capabilities in power systems and to formulate explicit prices of ramping capabilities. With the increasing penetration of renewable energy, demand-side resources become more important as the flexibility of traditional thermal generators is limited. In this paper, a real-time market model considering demand-side resources and a parametric programming method are proposed to analyze the potential of demand-side resources to provide flexible ramping products. The numerical results show the efficiency of demand-side resources to satisfy the system's ramping capability requirement and prove the effectiveness of the proposed model and method.

articleTitle: The Frequency Strength Evaluation Index Suitable for Scenario of High Proportion of Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the massive access of renewable energy, the frequency characteristics of the system have changed greatly. In the power system where the proportion of renewable energy is high, the frequency evaluation index obtained will no longer be applicable. Therefore, this paper proposed the frequency strength evaluation index suitable for high proportion renewable energy system. Firstly, the system frequency and the unified transfer function structure (UTFS) model are established. Secondly, the error of frequency strength evaluation index caused by using the index to evaluate frequency strength in different scenarios is analyzed. Furthermore, the frequency strength evaluation index used in high proportion renewable energy system is proposed and based on the proposed index, the frequency strength evaluation steps are given. Finally, the effectiveness of the index is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Directed-Graph-Based Distributed Data-Driven LFC Approach for Multi-Source Interconnected Power Systems in Energy Internet
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The power system is an important part of the energy internet, and its complexity has been a major challenge in modeling and control. To address the problem of frequency stability for multi-area interconnected power systems with an unknown model, a distributed load frequency control (LFC) scheme based on an adaptive data-driven algorithm is proposed. Firstly, a power system data model coupling information and energy flow connection is established by introducing dynamic linearization technology. Subsequently, a distributed data-driven controller with an adaptive gain is developed based on a directed graph, which reduces the dependence of controller design on accurate models. Meanwhile, an improved projection algorithm is given to adaptively update the pseudo-partial gain and the hetero-geneous condition of power system is considered. Additionally, the convergence of the system is proved by the compression mapping method. Finally, a simulation example is provided to prove that the proposed strategy can effectively regulate the frequency of multi-area interconnected power system.

articleTitle: Shapley Value-Based Profit Allocation Method for Flexible Resources of Virtual Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The high uncertainty associated with wind and photovoltaic power poses a great challenge to the secure operation of power systems. Utilizing flexible resources in all parts of power systems is an effective means to maintain the secure operation of power systems with high penetration of renewable energy. Since flexible resources mostly exist in the form of distributed energy resources (DERs), virtual power plant (VPP) is currently a novel business model to effectively aggregate DERs. To ensure the long-term viability of the business model of VPP, the profits obtained by the members within VPP must be fairly allocated. Therefore, it is crucial to investigate the profit allocation method of flexible resources within VPP. In this paper, the flexible resources in VPP are first modeled. A two-settlement bidding model for VPP participation in the day-ahead market (DAM) and the real-time market (RTM) is then designed. The Shapley value method is adopted to allocate the profits of flexible resources within VPP. The results of the algorithm demonstrate that the flexible resources can not only smooth the fluctuation of wind and photovoltaic power output but also improve their own profits as well as the overall profits of VPP. The proposed mechanism can incentivize increased participation of flexible resources within the power system in VPP, thereby proposing the advancement of VPP.

articleTitle: Review on Icing Growth Model for Overhead Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Icing on overhead transmission lines is one of the most serious threat to the safe and stable operation of power system. The occurrence of icing gives rise to a range of electrical and mechanical accidents, resulting in significant loss for the power system. This paper summarizes the research status of icing growth models in order to evaluate the icing conditions on these lines and ensure the safe and reliable operation of the power system. Firstly, ice disaster mechanism is summarized considering the formation of line icing, icing type and icing influencing factors. Secondly, it summarizes ice growth models and their limitations, starting with commonly used physics and machine learning models. Finally, the potential research directions for icing growth models in overhead transmission lines are discussed aiming to pave the way for future studies.

articleTitle: Three Strategies for Coordinating Multiple Resources for Frequency Control in Power Systems Considering Diverse Computing and Communication Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This paper presents three distinct strategies to improve the power grid frequency control with varying computing and communication capabilities of the distributed resources, such as wind power, photovoltaics (PV), and energy storage (ES). The first strategy, termed traditional virtual droop and inertial control, is suitable for resources with limited computing and communication capabilities. In situations where distributed resources possess strong communication but weak computing capabilities, the second strategy combines a virtual synchronous generator model with a proportional power sharing (PPS) strategy to propose the expected power and allocate it based on adjustable capacity. The third strategy caters to distributed resources with strong computing but weak communication capabilities, employing a control mechanism based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MA-DRL). The effectiveness of the proposed strategies is demonstrated through simulations of a two-region interconnected load frequency control system on the Matlab/Simulink platform, which maintains stable frequency even as the proportion of renewable energy increases.

articleTitle: Intelligent Inspection Route Planning Based On the Improved Ant-Lion Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The challenges of autonomous and joint inspection of intelligent equipment, such as Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and robots, in substations are constantly gaining attention. To efficiently capture high-quality images of power equipment, we propose a method for automatically generating joint inspection points for multiple intelligent equipment. It introduces a shooting potential model and a spatial relationship model to assess the suitability of shooting power equipment at different spatial points using various intelligent equipment. A point selection method is designed based on shooting quality constraints and spatial constraints to optimize inspection efficiency. The focus is on generating non-redundant and complete inspection points that are suitable for multiple intelligent equipment to perform with. Additionally, we study cooperative path planning of the heterogeneous robot systems to reduce the time required for the inspection task. An improved Ant-Lion Optimization Algorithm is proposed to decouple the routes of mobile robots and UAVs and plan their routes simultaneously. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated on a virtual substation experimental platform, revealing improvements in shooting quality, inspection efficiency, and reduced inspection time.

articleTitle: Economic Benefit Analysis of Flexibility Improvement of Coal-Fired Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In recent years, the proportion of renewable energy in the power system has been increasing. Due to the intermittent nature of renewable energy, there is an increasing demand for peak shaving and frequency regulation in power systems, and there is an urgent need for coal-fired power plants(CFPPs) to undergo flexibility retrofits to improve their peak shaving capacity. This paper discusses the restrictive factors of operating flexibility of CFPPs and the key technologies of unit flexibility retrofits. The cost of flexibility retrofitting of CFPPs is analyzed, including the costs of unit modification, the opportunity costs and the life loss costs of unit participation in peak shaving. The benefits of participating in peak shaving for CFPPs under different peak shaving settlement modes are analyzed. Case studies show that when CFPPs participate in deep peak shaving, the proportion of opportunity cost is relatively large. When the unit is in a deep peak shaving state that requires combustion support, the combustion support cost accounts for a proportion of the deep peak shaving cost. The quantity of the peak shaving volume of units has a significant impact on the average cost of peak shaving, and it is necessary for the units operator to have an optimal balance between daily power generation and participating in peak shaving. It is suggested that the government provide technical and financial support for the flexibility retrofits for CFPPs. Meanwhile, it is suggested to channel the costs of flexibility retrofits of CFPPs through market mechanisms.

articleTitle: Research on Decoupling Relationship among Energy Consumption, Carbon Emissions, and Economic Growth under Dual Carbon Goals in China
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The aspiration of reaching a carbon peak by 2030 and attaining carbon neutrality by 2060 is an inherent requirement for achieving high-quality development. This paper adopts the energy economy theory to construct an optimization model to predict future energy consumption trajectory and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions path in China. Furthermore, drawing upon the Tapio decoupling index methodology, we studied their decoupling characteristics. The results show that in the dynamic evolution process from energy consumption dual control to carbon dual control, energy consumption continues to exhibit an ascending trajectory in the foreseeable near to medium term in China, and a steady downward trend in the long term. Similar trends in carbon emissions. The period from 2020 to 2035 is a critical window for energy, economy, and carbon emissions to undergo decoupling in China. After 2035, China entered a stage of strong sustainable development. Between 2020 and 2040, the decoupling between energy intensity and carbon emission intensity remained stable but exhibited a relatively weak trend. After 2040, energy intensity and carbon emission intensity entered a phase of significant decoupling, marking China's successful transition from energy consumption dual control to carbon emissions dual control.

articleTitle: Review on Optimal Scheduling of Cascade Hydro-Wind-Solar-Pumped Storage Complementary System for the New Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Under the background of “carbon peaking and carbon neutrality”, the proportion of renewable energy such as wind and solar power generation is increasing year by year.
